title: st.tabs: know and control state
body:
### Problem

st.tabs is purely an organizational element with no access to know or control its state.

### Solution

Add an option (or new component) to make st.tabs an element that communicates with the backend to know and control state.

### Additional context

This is related to #5321 but a more robust feature request.
There is an ongoing thread in the forums on this topic. I'm creating this feature request for votes to be recorded.
https://<redacted-host>/t/st-tabs-is-it-possible-to-do-any-of-the-following-access-an-st-tab-click-event-set-a-default-selected-tab-on-a-page/29341

comments.body:
For anyone wanting an alternative, here is a [segmented control](https://www.google.com/search?q=segmented+control) component using buttons:

```py
def segmented_control(labels: list[str], key: str, default: str | None = None, max_size: int = 6) -> str:
    """Group of buttons with the given labels. Return the selected label."""
    if key not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state[key] = default or labels[0]

    selected_label = st.session_state[key]

    def set_label(label: str) -> None:
        st.session_state.update(**{key: label})

    cols = st.columns([1] * len(labels) + [max_size - len(labels)])

    for col, label in zip(cols, labels):
        btn_type = "primary" if selected_label == label else "secondary"
        col.button(label, on_click=set_label, args=(label,), use_container_width=True, type=btn_type)

    return selected_label
```

It can be used like this:

```py
selected = segmented_control(["A", "B", "C"], default="B", key="tabs")

if selected == "A":
    st.markdown("Content in A")
    st.button("Go to B", on_click=lambda: st.session_state.update(tabs="B"))

elif selected == "B":
    st.markdown("Content in B")
    st.button("Go to C", on_click=lambda: st.session_state.update(tabs="C"))

elif selected == "C":
    st.markdown("Content in C")
    st.button("Go to A", on_click=lambda: st.session_state.update(tabs="A"))
```

![segmented_control](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/89593325/2f26e3e8-4f06-46a9-b8c5-49ce3b8e1141)

comments.author: participant19
comments.body:
# Update

Hey all! We haven't started working on this issue yet. But in the next release, we will add selections for charts & dataframes (see #455), which will come with a pretty general new API pattern to control events in Streamlit. In that case, it will use a new `on_select` parameter that can be set to:

- `on_select="ignore"`, in which case Streamlit will not react to the (selection) event in any special way, i.e. it will not rerun. 
- `on_select="rerun"`, in which case Streamlit will rerun in response to a (selection) event and return the selection data. 
- `on_select=callback_func`, in which case Streamlit will first execute the callback function (similar to the existing `on_change` parameters) and then rerun. 

We'll probably extend this pattern to the issue here: we'll add one parameter (maybe `on_change` or something similar) to control whether Streamlit reruns in response to a tab change. If yes, `st.tabs` will return information about the selected tab. That part is still a bit tricky, though, since tabs currently return a container object, so we need to find a way to return the container + information on what was selected. Will update here once we have a better idea of how we're doing this. 

We're currently focusing on other projects though, so it will take a while before we get to it.

comments.author: participant43
comments.body:
An update on this 🗞️

Starting in **Streamlit 1.55**, `st.tabs` supports `on_change` and `key`, which lets you **know and control** tab state.

### Reading the current tab

Use `key` + `on_change="rerun"` to access the active tab label via `st.session_state`:

```python
import streamlit as st

tab1, tab2, tab3 = st.tabs(
    ["Overview", "Details", "Raw Data"],
    key="my_tabs",
    on_change="rerun",
)

# The active tab label is available in session state
st.write(f"Currently viewing: {st.session_state.my_tabs}")

# Each tab also has an .open property you can check
with tab1:
    if tab1.open:
        st.write("Overview is selected!")

with tab2:
    if tab2.open:
        st.write("Details is selected!")
```

Programmatically switching tabs

Set `st.session_state[key]` to switch to a different tab:

```
import streamlit as st

def switch_to_preview():
    st.session_state.my_tabs = "Preview"

tab1, tab2 = st.tabs(["Editor", "Preview"], key="my_tabs", on_change="rerun")

with tab1:
    content = st.text_area("Write something")
    st.button("Switch to Preview", on_click=switch_to_preview)

with tab2:
    st.markdown(content)
```
